process.process_name: Anti-reflective coating of optical lenses, batch vacuum deposition line

stages.name: Incoming inspection
stages.description: the operator visually inspects each lot of lens substrates for scratches, chips and contamination, and logs the lot number and findings.
stages.source_text: Incoming inspection: the operator visually inspects each lot of lens substrates for scratches, chips and contamination, and logs the lot number and findings.

stages.name: Ultrasonic cleaning
stages.description: the operator loads substrates into baskets, selects the cleaning recipe for the lot, and runs them through a multi-tank ultrasonic line.
stages.source_text: Ultrasonic cleaning: the operator loads substrates into baskets, selects the cleaning recipe for the lot, and runs them through a multi-tank ultrasonic line.

stages.name: Drying and fixturing
stages.description: after drying, the operator mounts substrates in the coating fixture (planetary dome) in a laminar-flow area, recording positions.
stages.source_text: Drying and fixturing: after drying, the operator mounts substrates in the coating fixture (planetary dome) in a laminar-flow area, recording positions.

stages.name: Recipe selection
stages.description: the process engineer selects the coating recipe (layer materials, thicknesses, deposition rates) from the recipe library and confirms it against the customer specification.
stages.source_text: Recipe selection: the process engineer selects the coating recipe (layer materials, thicknesses, deposition rates) from the recipe library and confirms it against the customer specification.

stages.name: Chamber loading and pump-down
stages.description: the operator loads the dome into the vacuum chamber and starts pump-down. The process waits until base pressure is reached.
stages.source_text: Chamber loading and pump-down: the operator loads the dome into the vacuum chamber and starts pump-down. The process waits until base pressure is reached.

stages.name: Deposition run
stages.description: e-beam evaporation with ion assist runs the layer sequence. The PLC controls shutters and rates, thickness is monitored by quartz crystal and optical monitoring, and the operator watches for deviations and can abort the run.
systems: E-beam evaporation system with ion assist
stages.source_text: Deposition run: e-beam evaporation with ion assist runs the layer sequence. The PLC controls shutters and rates, thickness is monitored by quartz crystal and optical monitoring, and the operator watches for deviations and can abort the run.

stages.name: Venting and unloading
stages.description: the chamber is vented, the dome cools, and the operator unloads the substrates.
stages.source_text: Venting and unloading: the chamber is vented, the dome cools, and the operator unloads the substrates.

stages.name: Optical QC
stages.description: witness samples are measured on a spectrophotometer, and reflectance is compared against the specification to give pass or fail.
stages.source_text: Optical QC: witness samples are measured on a spectrophotometer, and reflectance is compared against the specification to give pass or fail.

stages.name: Cosmetic inspection
stages.description: the operator inspects each lens under an inspection lamp for pinholes, haze and stains.
stages.source_text: Cosmetic inspection: the operator inspects each lens under an inspection lamp for pinholes, haze and stains.

stages.name: Disposition and records
stages.description: passing lots are released to packing. Failing lots go to rework (strip and recoat, returning to stage 2) or scrap. The batch record is completed for traceability.
outputs: Lots routed to rework or scrap

rework_to.when: failing lot is sent to rework (strip and recoat) instead of scrap

stages.source_text: Disposition and records: passing lots are released to packing. Failing lots go to rework (strip and recoat, returning to stage 2) or scrap. The batch record is completed for traceability.

assumptions: Stages are modelled as a sequence in the order numbered, since the text states no other ordering.
The strip step is part of the rework path, not a separate stage, because stages must match the numbered lines.
Scrap and release to packing are terminal outcomes of stage 10.
ambiguities: Where and when are witness samples loaded, and which stage produces them?
How many recipe confirmations take place before deposition, and who performs each?
Who performs the optical QC measurements and the disposition decision (operator, QC technician, quality engineer)?
What is the base pressure target and who confirms it has been reached?
Who decides between rework and scrap for failing lots, and on what criteria?
Does a cosmetic inspection failure also trigger rework or scrap, or only optical QC failures?
Can cosmetic inspection (stage 9) run in parallel with optical QC (stage 8)?
Where is the strip step performed, and does stripped material re-enter at stage 1 or stage 2?
What happens to a run aborted by the operator in stage 6 (partial coating, rework, scrap)?
Which records does the batch record contain, and in which system is it kept?

intervention.rationale: Camera-based defect detection for scratches, chips and contamination is well-defined and checkable. The operator keeps the accept/reject judgment and the AI drafts the log entry.

data_required: Labelled images of substrate defects by type
interfaces: Lot log or record system (currently unspecified)
integration.rationale: New imaging hardware and a labelled defect dataset must be collected. The log system is not named, so a lightweight record integration is needed.

failure_modes.description: A missed substrate defect (scratch or chip) passes into the line and is only discovered after coating, wasting a coating run on bad substrates.
Over-rejection of acceptable substrates causes unnecessary scrap or delay.

risk.regulatory_note: General quality-system and record expectations for the lot log.

assumptions: Defect acceptance criteria exist and can be written down
Substrates can be imaged at the inspection point
The lot log is a paper or simple digital record

intervention.rationale: AI could recommend the cleaning recipe from lot data and flag mismatches, while the operator does the physical loading and runs the line. Selection is a bounded sub-task.

data_required: Lot data and substrate type from stage 1
interfaces: Cleaning line controller or recipe selector (interface unknown)
integration.rationale: Recommendation is advisory, but reading line parameters needs one system integration whose interface is not stated.

failure_modes.description: A wrong cleaning recipe recommendation that is not caught leaves contamination or damages substrates, causing coating adhesion or cosmetic failures found later.

risk.regulatory_note: General quality-system and record expectations for recipe records.

assumptions: Cleaning recipes are stored digitally or can be digitised
The line exposes parameters through a PLC or export
Rework lots re-entering here may need a different recipe

intervention.rationale: A camera could verify fixture loading and capture substrate positions automatically for the record. Mounting in a laminar-flow area is manual work that stays with the operator.

interfaces: Camera in or near the laminar-flow area
integration.rationale: New camera capture in a cleanliness-controlled area and a position-record integration are required.

failure_modes.description: Incorrect position record misattributes substrates to dome positions, undermining traceability and later root-cause analysis.
Added equipment or handling in the laminar-flow area introduces particulate contamination.

risk.regulatory_note: Position records support traceability and may be audited or customer-mandated.

assumptions: Position recording is currently manual
Customers expect traceability from lot to dome position
Camera placement does not disturb laminar flow

intervention.rationale: Matching a recipe from the library against the customer specification is digital and checkable. AI can propose and cross-check, while the process engineer remains accountable for confirmation.

data_required: Recipe library with layer materials, thicknesses and rates
integration.rationale: Data is digital, but the recipe library and specification formats need extraction and cleaning.

failure_modes.description: A wrong or outdated recipe is confirmed against the specification, so a full run is coated incorrectly and defective lenses may reach the customer.
Misreading the customer specification leads to a mismatch that is detected only at optical QC.

risk.regulatory_note: Customer-mandated controls and recipe traceability are likely, but no regulation is named in the model.

assumptions: Specifications are available as text or structured documents
Recipe library has version control
The ambiguity on how many confirmations occur before deposition is unresolved

intervention.rationale: AI could monitor pump-down curves, flag leaks or abnormal pumping behaviour and predict time to base pressure. Loading the dome and starting pump-down remain manual.

interfaces: Vacuum gauge and pumping system data (PLC or historian)
integration.rationale: Read-only data capture from the pumping system is one integration. No control authority is assumed.

failure_modes.description: A missed leak or abnormal pump-down signal lets a run start with poor vacuum, degrading coating quality across the lot.
Nuisance alerts delay the process and cause alarm fatigue.

assumptions: Pressure data is available electronically
Base pressure target is defined, though the model leaves it unspecified
AI role is advisory only, with no control of valves or pumps

intervention.rationale: AI could watch rate, thickness and optical monitor signals for drift or deviation and alert the operator. Control and abort authority stay with the PLC and operator.

interfaces: PLC data export or OPC-style gateway (unspecified)
integration.rationale: Several systems and real-time data limits are involved. Read-only monitoring avoids safety-rated control, but data access and calibration are substantial. Because a missed deviation or a wrong abort is irreversible, any AI recommendation to continue or abort needs operator approval before action.

failure_modes.description: A missed deviation allows a mis-thickness or contaminated coating to complete, losing the production run or letting a defect reach the customer.
A false alarm prompts an unnecessary operator abort and wastes a run.

risk.regulatory_note: Run data may be needed for batch traceability, but the model names no regulation.

assumptions: PLC and monitors can export data at useful rates
AI has no write access to the PLC, shutters or e-beam
Handling of aborted runs is unresolved in the model

intervention.rationale: Venting, cooling and unloading are physical handling steps with little decision content. Any AI role would be marginal, so none is appropriate.

integration.rationale: No AI integration is proposed. Chamber data could be logged but the stage adds little value.

failure_modes.description: Mishandling during unloading chips or scratches coated lenses, or venting too early thermally shocks substrates.

assumptions: Venting is a standard automated or manual chamber sequence
Cooling criteria are fixed by procedure

intervention.rationale: Spectrophotometer data is digital, and comparing reflectance against a specification is well-defined and checkable. AI can compute pass or fail and flag borderline results for a person to confirm.

data_required: Witness sample identity and run linkage
integration.rationale: Instrument output is digital and an export likely exists. Linking witness samples to runs is unresolved and may need new data capture.

failure_modes.description: A false pass on out-of-specification reflectance releases defective lenses to the customer.
A false fail sends good lots to rework or scrap, costing time and material.

risk.regulatory_note: Customer-mandated QC records and traceability are likely; no regulation is named.

assumptions: The model names no actor for this stage, so a QC technician or engineer is assumed to supervise
Witness samples are linked to the lot, though the origin of witness samples is unresolved
Measurement is already digital

intervention.rationale: Machine vision under controlled lighting can detect pinholes, haze and stains and assist the operator. Findings are visual and checkable, but defect criteria need to be collected.

data_required: Labelled images of pinholes, haze and stains
interfaces: Imaging station replacing or augmenting the inspection lamp
integration.rationale: New imaging hardware, controlled lighting and labelled data collection are required. Haze and stains can be hard to image reliably. Because a missed defect reaching the customer is irreversible, the operator approves each accept decision before lenses move on.

failure_modes.description: A missed cosmetic defect on a coated lens reaches the customer.
Over-flagging increases rework or scrap and slows throughput.

risk.regulatory_note: General quality-system and record expectations; customer cosmetic standards may apply.

assumptions: Cosmetic criteria are defined, though the model does not specify them
Whether a cosmetic failure triggers rework or scrap is unresolved
The 4 rating assumes the human gives the final accept on AI findings

intervention.rationale: AI can compile QC results into the batch record, check completeness and recommend release, rework or scrap. The decision and accountability for release stay with a person.

integration.rationale: Several records must be consolidated into the batch record, whose system is not named. The disposition decision and its criteria are unresolved.

failure_modes.description: Wrongly releasing a failing lot sends defective lenses to the customer.
Incomplete or incorrect batch record breaks traceability for audit or complaint investigation.
Wrong rework versus scrap choice wastes a recoverable lot or sends an unrecoverable lot through strip and recoat.

risk.regulatory_note: The batch record is kept for traceability, which suggests audited records or customer-mandated controls; no regulation is named.

assumptions: The model names no actor, so a quality engineer is assumed to be accountable
Rework and scrap criteria are unresolved
Rework path returns to stage 2 as stated

executive_summary: This is a provisional analysis of 'Anti-reflective coating of optical lenses, batch vacuum deposition line' covering 10 stages. Tier 1 starting points, by the ranking formula: 1 (Incoming inspection), 4 (Recipe selection). No appropriate AI role was found for: 7 (Venting and unloading). Low-confidence analyses, which depend on open questions: 5 (Chamber loading and pump-down), 6 (Deposition run), 8 (Optical QC), 10 (Disposition and records). Scores are model judgments for engineer review; see the limitations.

priorities.rationale: Tier 1: fit 4/5, effort 3/5, worst-case severity 3/5 (partial), human check review_after, confidence medium.
Tier 1: fit 4/5, effort 2/5, worst-case severity 4/5 (partial), human check approve_before, confidence medium.
Tier 2: fit 3/5, effort 3/5, worst-case severity 3/5 (partial), human check approve_before, confidence medium.
Tier 2: fit 3/5, effort 3/5, worst-case severity 3/5 (partial), human check review_after, confidence medium.
Tier 2: fit 3/5, effort 3/5, worst-case severity 3/5 (partial), human check review_after, confidence low.
Tier 2: fit 4/5, effort 2/5, worst-case severity 4/5 (irreversible), human check approve_before, confidence low.
Tier 3: fit 4/5, effort 3/5, worst-case severity 4/5 (irreversible), human check approve_before, confidence medium.
Tier 3: fit 3/5, effort 3/5, worst-case severity 4/5 (irreversible), human check approve_before, confidence low.
Tier 3: fit 3/5, effort 4/5, worst-case severity 4/5 (irreversible), human check approve_before, confidence low.
No AI role: Venting, cooling and unloading are physical handling steps with little decision content. Any AI role would be marginal, so none is appropriate.

cross_cutting_risks: Severe failure modes (severity 4 or more) occur at stages 4 (Recipe selection), 6 (Deposition run), 8 (Optical QC), 9 (Cosmetic inspection), 10 (Disposition and records); a human check is needed before AI output takes effect there.

Audited records or customer-mandated controls (regulatory exposure 3 or more) apply at stages 3 (Drying and fixturing), 4 (Recipe selection), 6 (Deposition run), 8 (Optical QC), 10 (Disposition and records).
Stages 5 (Chamber loading and pump-down), 6 (Deposition run), 8 (Optical QC), 10 (Disposition and records) rest on unresolved questions, so their scores may change.

limitations:
- Scores are judgments made by a language model on anchored 1-5 scales, applied to a process description written by people. They are a structured starting point for review by a process engineer, not measurements.
- The priority tiers come from a simple formula (fit minus effort minus worst-case severity, with a penalty for irreversible failures). Its weights are not calibrated against real deployments. It has no benefit term, so it ranks feasibility and risk and not value. It gives no credit for human oversight and ignores the analyst's confidence.
- The analysis shows where AI could act. It does not size benefits, cost or schedule, and it does not validate any design.
- Accountability for the process, the safety envelope, quality obligations and the decision to deploy stays with the process owner.
- This analysis is PROVISIONAL: the process model has not been approved by a named person, and the open questions below remain to be resolved.
- Human oversight constraint applied: mandatory.
